title: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold first three-way summit at APEC in Shenzhen next week
dek: The White House says nuclear arms reduction will top the agenda and Ukraine will not be on it; the Kremlin says Ukraine will be discussed. India, with deep stakes in all three relationships, will not be in the room.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
US President Donald Trump, Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin plan to hold their first-ever three-way meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in the southern Chinese city of Shenzhen next week, the White House confirmed on Friday. It would be the first time the leaders of the world's three largest nuclear powers have met together.

The White House says the main subject will be cutting nuclear arsenals, after the last US-Russia arms-control treaty expired in February, and that the war with Iran may come up. It says the war in Ukraine will not be on the three-way agenda. Moscow has given a different account: according to reports, Kremlin aide Yuri Ushakov said Mr Trump and Mr Putin would hold in-depth talks on a Ukraine settlement in Shenzhen, without Ukraine or European governments present.

## What happened

White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales said in a statement that "the president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world." A senior US official, briefing reporters on condition of anonymity, called the meeting the "beginning of hopefully a conversation" on nuclear disarmament and said no agreement was expected, according to reports.

According to reports, Mr Trump will arrive in Shenzhen late on Wednesday for the two-day summit of APEC's 21 member economies, hold bilateral talks with Mr Xi on Thursday, and end his visit to China with the three-way meeting. Mr Putin is also due to attend APEC on 18-19 November. Before that, Mr Trump is due at the ASEAN summits in Manila on Tuesday, where Prime Minister Narendra Modi will also be present.

Beijing has been careful in public. Asked about the plan at Friday's regular briefing, Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Mao Ning said: "China is in communication with relevant parties regarding a meeting between the three heads of state." Chinese state media reported on Friday that Mr Xi would hold "bilateral" talks on the sidelines, but had not reported on the three-way meeting by Saturday morning, according to reports.

## Background

The New START treaty, which capped the deployed strategic warheads of the United States and Russia, expired in February 2026, leaving no treaty limits on the two largest arsenals for the first time in decades. Mr Trump has said he wants any new arrangement to include China. The Pentagon estimates that China now has more than 600 nuclear warheads and is building more; Beijing has long refused to join arms-control talks, arguing that its arsenal is far smaller than those of the US and Russia.

The three leaders have been meeting in pairs for most of the year. Mr Xi hosted both Mr Putin and Mr Trump in Beijing earlier in 2026, and Mr Trump hosted Mr Xi in Washington in September, according to reports. Thursday's bilateral would be the fourth Trump-Xi meeting since 2025.

The meeting also comes a day after US and Russian officials met over Ukraine. US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner saw Mr Putin in Moscow on Thursday, after talks in Abu Dhabi produced agreement on a large prisoner exchange but no deal on territory.

## What they are saying

Ukraine's foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, said the summit would only "encourage Putin to continue this war", according to reports. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has voiced concern that the meeting could be used to settle Ukraine's future without Kyiv.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov called such a meeting "extremely significant", according to reports, but rejected comparisons with the 1945 Yalta conference, at which the wartime Allied leaders divided post-war Europe, and said any agreements reached could not be imposed on others. Earlier this month he said there were "signals confirming readiness" for three-way talks.

Germany's President Frank-Walter Steinmeier has said Mr Xi has no interest in discussing Russia's war against Ukraine, according to reports. Some reports, citing the Wall Street Journal, say Mr Putin proposed the three-way meeting in the hope of securing peace terms more favourable to Russia; the Kremlin has not said so.

## Why it matters for India

India has major interests in each of the three relationships on the table, and a seat at none of them.

- **Russia:** India is one of the largest buyers of Russian crude oil and relies on Russia for much of its military equipment. A US law passed in September, the Sanctioning Russia Act, allows tariffs of up to 100% on the biggest buyers of Russian oil, a list that includes India and China, according to reports. Any US-Russia understanding on Ukraine would change how much that threat matters.
- **China:** India faces China across the disputed Line of Actual Control and depends on Chinese supplies of electronics, solar equipment, drug ingredients and rare earths. China this week extended its pause on rare-earth export curbs only until 10 January. A warmer US-China relationship could ease supply pressures, or could leave India negotiating with Beijing from a weaker position.
- **Nuclear arms:** India is not part of any arms-control framework that limits the US, Russia or China. A three-way conversation that eventually turns to Chinese warhead numbers would bear directly on India's own nuclear planning, since China is the main reference point for India's deterrent.
- **Trade with the US:** India is still negotiating an interim trade deal with Washington. Commerce Secretary Rajesh Agrawal said on Friday that the talks were "on the right track", and the US has reportedly assured India of lower tariffs than its regional competitors; neither government has confirmed the terms.

The Ministry of External Affairs has not commented on the Shenzhen meeting. At Thursday's weekly briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said only that he would keep reporters updated on developments in Manila, including on a possible Quad leaders' meeting.

## What happens next

- **16-18 November:** Mr Modi in Manila for the 23rd ASEAN-India Summit and the 21st East Asia Summit; a Quad leaders' meeting and a Modi-Trump bilateral have been reported as possible but are unconfirmed.
- **17 November (Tuesday):** Mr Trump due at the ASEAN summits in Manila, according to reports.
- **18-19 November:** APEC leaders' meetings in Shenzhen; Trump-Xi bilateral on Thursday, followed by the three-way meeting.
- **14-15 December:** the US hosts the G20 summit in Miami.

The White House has not said whether a joint statement will follow the three-way meeting. US officials have said they do not expect any agreement.
